dataset.name: Sources and Variability of Nitrate on an Alaskan Hillslope Dominated by Alder Shrubs, Kougarok, Alaska, 2017 and 2018
description: Data provided include results of analyses of soil pore-water, soil moisture, and leaf litter samples collected at a Kougarok Hillslope site dominated by alder shrubs (KG_MM64) in the Seward Peninsula, Alaska during July and September 2017 and 2018. Samples were from surface soils in close proximity to 5 alder patches, collected upslope, within, and downslope of the alder patches. Pore water was analyzed for a comprehensive set of anions, cations, elemental analyses, and oxygen and nitrogen isotopes. Soil samples were collected for soil moisture determination. Leaf litter extracts were analyzed for carbon and nitrogen content and carbon and nitrogen isotopes. This dataset contains 3 *.csv files and 1 *.pdf file.

The Next-Generation Ecosystem Experiments: Arctic (NGEE Arctic), was a research effort to reduce uncertainty in Earth System Models by developing a predictive understanding of carbon-rich Arctic ecosystems and feedbacks to climate. NGEE Arctic was supported by the Department of Energy's Office of Biological and Environmental Research. The NGEE Arctic project had two field research sites: 1) located within the Arctic polygonal tundra coastal region on the Barrow Environmental Observatory (BEO) and the North Slope near Utqiagvik (Barrow), Alaska and 2) multiple areas on the discontinuous permafrost region of the Seward Peninsula north of Nome, Alaska. Through observations, experiments, and synthesis with existing datasets, NGEE Arctic provided an enhanced knowledge base for multi-scale modeling and contributed to improved process representation at global pan-Arctic scales within the Department of Energy's Earth system Model (the Energy Exascale Earth System Model, or E3SM), and specifically within the E3SM Land Model component (ELM).

measurementTechnique: Soil Pore Water SamplingFor soil pore water collection, rhizons were installed within the top 30 cm of soil and connected to 60 mL syringes. Rhizons were left to collect water overnight, water was extracted daily, and syringes were rehung. Bulk Soil CollectionFor bulk soil collection, samples were collected in tins from 15 to 60 cm depth (bottom of the collection tin). Rocks, large roots, and debris were removed from soil prior to sealing tin. The moisture content was determined by loss of weight upon drying. Leaf Litter CollectionLeaf litter samples were collected by hand from the ground surface and placed into plastic bags for preservation. Leaf litter was leached and analyzed using an elemental analyzer and isotope ratio mass spectrometry. Thaw Depth MeasurementDepth of soil to rock or frozen ground was collected by inserting a steel probe into the ground three times and averaging the three depths recorded. LocationsLocation measurements were taken with a handheld GPS (plus/minus 3m accuracy) using NAD 83 UTM Zone 4N.AnalysesLaboratory analyses were performed using EPA and other standard published methods.Cation concentrations were measured by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (Optima 2100 DV; PerkinElmer, USA) following US EPA Method 200.7. Inorganic anion concentrations were measured by ion chromatography (DX-600; Dionex, USA) following US EPA Method 300.0. Hydrogen and oxygen stable water isotopes were measured using an Isoprime continuous-flow isotope ratio mass spectrometer (GV Instruments, UK). Samples were analyzed for aqueous nitrate nitrogen and oxygen isotope ratios using a modified version of the microbial denitrification technique described by Casciotti et al. (2002) and Sigman et al. (2001) and measured using a GV Instruments Isoprime mass spectrometer coupled to a TraceGas peripheral instrument.
